name: Trak Starz
notes: The busiest hat part in this batch and the emptiest harmony, which is the whole shape of the record: "busy 16th hats with 32nd rolls" over "a minor pentatonic riff over a static i; no chord support". So the hats are `continuous` with the highest `fillDensity` here and the highest `hihat.rolls.freqPerBar` bar one, `scales` narrows to `minor_pentatonic` first, and ⛔ `chords.impliedByRiff` is set — a description rather than an exemption, since the research says there is no chord support at all. The chord part's variety therefore comes from a wide `chordDurationBeats`, three `harmonicRhythm` values and a wide voicing register rather than from progressions this duo does not play; the i–VII pair is INFERRED and weighted accordingly. The tambourine sits on the offbeats exactly as written, which is `percs.placement: offbeat`, and the melody is the bright mono lead the research names — 1–2 bar loop, mid-high, `monophonicBias` 1. ⚠ The vocal-chant counter-layer the research describes is modelled as a low-register `octave_echo` counter; the engine has no vocal timbre and this is an approximation rather than a reading. ⚠ `low`, the research's medium-low: the credit and era are sourced, the paragraph says the parameters are inferred and marks the 76–84 half-time band (stored as its 152–168 straight equivalent) LOW-CONF. ⚠ `fills.snareRollLadder` is off — with both fill periods at 4 bars the big fill wins and the inherited climbing ladder reads no seed, so it would write one identical fill on every one of 200; the 32nd roll that replaces it is the fill this paragraph actually names. ⚠ `anticipationProb` raised to 0.15. With `mirror_kick` against a fully locked 808 both parts take every kick, so every bass onset lands exactly on an 808 onset — `coherence.rs` calls that one line played twice rather than two parts locking. The lock is the style and is untouched; the anticipation is what makes them two parts. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [1,2], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count.
